Q: Can an iOS app rely on iCloud Drive to finish syncing files after the app is suspended or terminated? A:

iOS does not guarantee that an actual scheduled background task will run for sure. Save edits and media locally before returning success. iCloud Drive handles file transfer, but does not, however, provide atomic records sync. Cloud kit is likely the more appropriate choice for structured records, although the app also needs a durable local queue and retries as well. BGTaskScheduler can provide additional opportunities, but not assured execution.

Q: Is something wrong with zeros or multiple pairs in stroke-dasharray? A:

The answers by Mike and enxaneta mention two things:

  • The sum of dashes and gaps can be slightly bigger than the circumference, and push the last zero-dash beyond the end.

  • So can the dash offset.

My observation is, that the latter is more important.

The example given by enxaneta works:

stroke-dashoffset="-293.214"
stroke-dasharray="0 146.607 293.214 146.607 0 146.607 0 146.607"

The sum of the dashes and gaps is 879.642 — slightly below 2·π·140 = 879.6459...

The unit 146.607 is exactly that sum divided by 6.

The positive equivalent of that offset is 586.428 (4 units).

With offsets 586.429 ... 586.654 the right circle disappears.

That range corresponds to a length of 0.226.

Offsets 0.001 ... 0.226 have the same effect.

I was wrong with my assumption, that the problem does not appear for the simpler pattern, as seen in the code sample below. Here the right circle disappears for offsets 0.001 ... 0.916.

The given intervals are for FF. In Chrome the last one goes to 1.008.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="200" height="200" viewBox="-50 -50 300 300">
  
  <circle cx="100" cy="100" r="100" 
          stroke-dasharray="0 78.539"
          stroke-dashoffset="0.001"
          style="fill: none; stroke-width: 76.536686473; stroke: purple; stroke-linecap: round;"
  />

</svg>

This simply seems to boil down to the fact, that there is a small danger zone after the origin on the right. When a dash lands in it, its linecaps disappear. I see no way to calculate the length of this danger zone. (It is not just the actual circumference minus the sum of dashes and gaps.)

BTW: The screenshot above shows two circles missing. But that was not in the browser. That must be some bug in librsvg. Nothing we should care about.
